title: Open Circuit
designBriefSource: The requested six-family planning batch; private prompt retained outside distribution.
goal: Collect the gem at (4,1,0) after recovering the enclosure.
stageDependency: Align the six-member body -> traverse from inside its protected cavity -> leave onto the upper bay -> approach its outside face -> recover it leftward -> use the northern rim for the final gem-clearing push.
planningBurden: The opening and protruding member affect both passage clearance and later input access. Parking must be assessed together with the next approach.
changedConstraints: An asymmetric six-member enclosure replaces the five-member source cavity.
The route changes from protected interior operation to an exterior leftward return.
A member still covers the gem after recovery, requiring another useful input.
physicalScope: One 16 by 16 room; ordinary pinned official engine; all initial actors at elevation zero.

difficulty.qualification: An author estimate from dependent operations and planning tradeoffs, not calibrated human difficulty.

limits: Rightward operation before later leftward recovery is necessary under the stated exclusion.
An extra push destroys the planned input but is recoverable; its saved repair route refutes an exact-parking or unavoidable-dead-end claim.
The witness uses a final right push; that exact last push is not claimed necessary across all histories.
